what: Extend catalog search so '2:255', '2 255', '٢:٢٥٥', 'kahf 10', 'p293' and 'juz 30' jump straight to the ayah, page or juz, with the parsed target shown as the first result. search.ts matches surah titles and transliterations but not references.
why: Ayah reviewers single out 'searching any ayah in the surah:ayah format' (https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/ayah-quran-app/id706037876). It is the fastest path from hearing an ayah cited in a khutbah to reading it.

title: Remember recent searches and jumps
what: Show the last 8 searches and jumps as chips under the search field. Store them locally, with a one-tap clear.
why: An open quran_android request (#447 'remember last search queries', https://github.com/quran/quran_android/issues). It cuts the repeat-lookup path to a single tap.

title: Private notes on an ayah
what: Attach a plain-text note to any ayah or page, stored in IndexedDB and included in the backup file. Notes appear as a small dot in the margin, outside the text, and are listed on a Notes screen grouped by surah.
why: 'add notes to an ayah' is quran_android #37 with 17 comments and still open years later (https://github.com/quran/quran_android/issues). Keeping notes on the device suits the privacy pitch: personal reflections never touch a server.

title: Coloured bookmark groups that collapse
what: Let bookmarks carry one of five colours or a named group (Hifz, Ruqyah, Duas, Khutbah), with groups that collapse on the Bookmarks list. Bookmarks are page-only today ('Bookmark this page').
why: Ayah lists 'colorful bookmarks and starred verses' as a selling point (https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/ayah-quran-app/id706037876). quran_android has two open requests to collapse tag groups (#2522, #1342).

title: Reciter playlists and drag-to-reorder favourites
what: Let readers drag-reorder favourite reciters, and build a playlist such as Kahf by Budair, then Mulk by Juhany, then Sudais from 1447 that plays as one queue on the lock screen.
why: Open quran_android requests #1448 ('Allow users to rearrange reciters') and #1891 ('Listening multiple reciters consecutively with preset order') (https://github.com/quran/quran_android/issues). This catalogue is reciter- and mosque-year-heavy, so ordering matters more here than in a single-reciter app.

title: Arabic-plus-English recitation as a 'reciter'
what: Add archive.org's per-surah 'Mishary + Ibrahim Walk (Sahih International)' sets, which interleave ayah and translation, as a catalogue entry tagged 'with English'. Range and ETag need checking first. Urdu equivalents (e.g. Sudais + Urdu) can be added the same way if archive.org hosts them per surah.
why: Open quran_android requests #641 ('Arabic recitation with English translation') and #908 (https://github.com/quran/quran_android/issues). Converts and children listening in the car ask for this most, and it is pure catalogue data with no code.

title: Cast to a speaker or TV
what: Add a Cast button on the player using the Remote Playback API (audio.remote.prompt()), which Chrome on Android supports for <audio> and so also works in the TWA. Hide it when remote.watchAvailability reports no devices.
why: quran_android #900 'Chromecast support' is open (https://github.com/quran/quran_android/issues). Families play Quran on the living-room speaker. This needs no SDK and no server.

title: Starter pack: Juz Amma in under 40 MB on first run
what: After onboarding, offer one card: 'Keep Juz Amma + Yasin + Mulk + Kahf offline (about 38 MB) with <default reciter>'. It downloads in the background through the existing chunked queue, and big downloads stay opt-in.
why: quran_android #1994 (first download in the background) and #936 (small sound files) (https://github.com/quran/quran_android/issues). It gives a new user offline value on day one without asking them to commit GBs.

title: Onboarding ends on the first recitation playing
what: Replace the 'which mushaf' step with 'Choose a voice'. Show four reciter faces with one-tap 10-second previews (Fatihah). Finishing onboarding starts Al-Fatihah in that voice, so the reader hears recitation within 15 seconds of install. The mushaf edition stays in Settings, since Onboarding.tsx itself says it is the choice users care least about.
why: Most uninstalls happen in the first session. Reviews praise apps for 'tens of reciters' (https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/ayah-quran-app/id706037876), and audio is this app's moat, so it should come first.

title: 'Nothing leaves your phone' privacy receipt
what: Add a Privacy screen under More that lists the only hosts the app can reach (taken from the CSP connect-src and media-src), what each is used for (audio files only), and a live local counter of requests made this session. It ends with: 'No account, no analytics, no ads. This is enforced by the page's security policy, not just promised.'
why: Muslim Pro's 2020 location-data scandal led a council of 90 New York mosques to urge members to delete it (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/11/18/muslim-pro-app-denies-selling-user-data-to-us-military). AlfaazPlus QuranApp puts 'no analytics or tracking' at the top of its pitch (https://github.com/alfaazplus/QuranApp). Showing proof beats making a claim.

title: Store listing that leads with 'no ads, no account'
what: Rewrite the 80-character short description and the first screenshot caption around what users complain about elsewhere: 'Free Quran audio & mushaf. No ads. No account. Works offline.' The second screenshot should be the reciter wall, the third talqeen or veil. Mirror this in the Arabic, Urdu and Indonesian listings.
why: The dominant complaint about Quran Majeed is heavy, non-skippable ads, even from paying users (https://chrome-stats.com/d/id365557665, https://ca.trustpilot.com/review/quranmajeed.com). For Tarteel it is the subscription paywall (https://justuseapp.com/en/app/1391009396/tarteel-recite-al-quran/reviews). Being free is this app's differentiator, and the current listing says it only in the body text.

title: Free 'recite back' check without AI
what: In Talqeen or Veil, a Record button captures the reader's own recitation of the range with MediaRecorder, kept locally. Playback alternates: their line, then the reciter's line, using the word timings, so they hear their own mistakes. Nothing is uploaded or auto-graded, so it never falsely marks a correct recitation wrong.
why: Tarteel's most consistent complaints are that mistake detection is paywalled and that it flags 'undeserved' errors (https://kimola.com/reports/unlock-insights-tarteel-quran-memorization-app-feedback-report-google-play-en-gb-156338, https://justuseapp.com/en/app/1391009396/tarteel-recite-al-quran/reviews). This gives the free, private, honest version that the roadmap's 'no AI checking' stance allows.

title: Family khatm by link
what: A 'Split a khatm' screen assigns the 30 juz across N named people and produces one link with the plan in the URL fragment (#khatm=...). Each person opens it, picks their name, and their juz becomes their wird with a resume point. There is no server, so no completion tracking, just the assignment.
why: Group khatms for Ramadan, Jumu'ah and after a death are a common practice that currently runs on WhatsApp lists. The app becomes the thing everyone in the group installs, which is growth without ads.
where: new src/ui/KhatmPanel.tsx, wird engine in src/hifz/schedule.ts, hash routing in src/App.tsx

title: Teacher sends a sabaq by link
what: A teacher marks sabaq, sabqi and manzil ranges on their own board and taps 'Send to student', which produces a link carrying the assignment in the fragment. The student's board imports it with a single confirm. This fits the roadmap rule that 'the app never sets your curriculum, your teacher does'.
why: It turns every hifz teacher into a distributor of the app to a whole class, with no server and no accounts.

title: Long-press icon shortcuts
what: Add manifest shortcuts (Bubblewrap turns them into Android app shortcuts): Continue listening, Surah al-Kahf, Juz Amma, Sleep listening (30-minute timer). The vite manifest has no 'shortcuts' today.
why: It brings the most frequent Friday and night actions down to one gesture from the home screen. It is free to add and the kind of polish reviewers notice in 'clean and fast' apps (https://www.fiveprayer.app/blog/best-quran-apps-complete-review).

title: Friday Kahf card on Home
what: From Thursday Maghrib to Friday Maghrib (approximated from device time), Home shows one card: 'Al-Kahf: continue at ayah 46 / 110', with read or listen buttons. It disappears when finished. No push notifications, no flame.
why: Reading Kahf on Friday is the most common weekly Quran habit, and Quran Majeed even sells a 'Surah Kahf' edition of its app (https://marlvel.ai/apps/quran-majeed-surah-kahf/vs). This keeps the roadmap's anti-streak stance.

title: Calendar reminder file for the wird
what: A TWA cannot schedule local notifications without a push server. Instead, 'Remind me daily' produces an .ics recurring event (e.g. 21:30, 'Juz 12 tonight', with the app's deep link) that the phone's own calendar raises.
why: quran_android has an open reminder-notifications request (https://github.com/quran/quran_android/issues). This meets it while keeping the no-backend constraint.

title: Keep the screen on while reading or in talqeen
what: Request a Screen Wake Lock while the mushaf, translation view or talqeen is in the foreground, release it on idle or background, and add a setting. The wakeLock API is not used anywhere in src/.
why: Reviewers praise being able to 'enlarge the text while praying' (https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/ayah-quran-app/id706037876). A screen that dims mid-page during qiyam or a halaqa is a constant small irritation.

title: Text size control for translation and Arabic
what: Add an A- / A+ control (or pinch) on the translation tab that scales the Arabic and translation independently, saved in prefs. Add a 'Large' preset in onboarding for older readers. It works by setting CSS variables, not by re-rendering.
why: Ayah reviewers specifically praise enlarging text (https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/ayah-quran-app/id706037876). Older family members are a large share of daily readers. MushafView already reads the computed font size, so the layout supports scaling.

title: Transliteration line for new Muslims and children
what: Add Tanzil's en.transliteration as an optional line between the Arabic and the translation, styled smaller and lighter.
why: Transliteration is a standard selling point of Muslim Pro and Quran Majeed for converts and non-Arabic-reading children. The app already sells on 'Translation tab is live'. It is pure data from the same Tanzil source, under the same non-commercial terms.

title: Indonesian, Turkish, Bengali and Malay translations
what: Add Tanzil's id.indonesian (Kemenag), tr.diyanet, bn.bengali and ms.basmeih as lazy-loaded editions, and add Indonesian and Bengali UI strings.
why: The app ships ar/en/fr/hi/ur, missing the two largest Muslim populations (Indonesia, Bangladesh). Ayah reviewers explicitly ask for Turkish and Dutch (https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/ayah-quran-app/id706037876). Each language added opens a new store-search audience at zero ad cost.
where: data/translations.json, public/trans, src/i18n/ (new id.ts, bn.ts), store/LISTING.md

title: Second tafsir: Jalalayn alongside Muyassar
what: Add Tanzil's ar.jalalayn as a second Arabic tafsir, shown in the same expandable slot as ar-muyassar, with a short 'What is this tafsir?' note.
why: Ayah got angry reviews when it removed Tafsir al-Muyassar ('تفسير الميسر أُزيل من التطبيق') (https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/ayah-quran-app/id706037876), which shows how much readers value even a short tafsir. Jalalayn is short and classical, and Tanzil hosts it as a downloadable file.

title: Never silently remove a translation or reciter
what: Once a translation or reciter has been downloaded, it stays on the device even if a later catalog drops it. The entry is shown as 'Retired: still on your phone' with the reason, instead of disappearing.
why: Ayah's 1-star reviews include 'why did you remove the english translation after this last update?' (https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/ayah-quran-app/id706037876). The Clear Quran (en-itani) licensing issue means this app will likely face exactly this situation.

title: Quiet listening history, measured as hours not flames
what: A private 'This month' card shows hours listened, pages read and surahs completed, as a small bar per week. It has no streak count and no badge, and resets nothing if a day is missed. It is computed from local play events and included in the backup.
why: quran_android #3018 asks for 'read history and charts' (https://github.com/quran/quran_android/issues). Quran.com users complain that its reading history 'skips verses and totals are incorrect' (https://feedback.quran.com/bugs/p/reading-history-skips-verses-and-totals-are-incorrect), so an accurate, local version is a real win. It respects the roadmap's anti-streak rule.

title: Resume points that never jump to the start of the surah
what: Give each reciter and surah its own resume point, remembered to within about 2 seconds and rewound slightly (about 3 s) on return. The resume card says 'Al-Baqarah 142, 1:04:12 with Budair'. Opening a bookmark goes to the exact ayah, not the top of the surah.
why: Quran.com's tracker is full of 'bookmarks opening to start of the surah' and 'Improve Last Read' bugs (https://feedback.gtaf.org/quran/p/bookmarks-opening-to-start-of-the-surah, https://feedback.gtaf.org/quran/p/improve-last-read-bugs-ux-issues). HomeResume already exists, so this widens it from one global point to one per surah.

title: Show the app at the masjid: printable QR poster
what: A More > Share the app screen shows a large QR code for the Play listing plus the web link, and a one-tap printable A4 poster (Arabic and English) for a masjid noticeboard. Two people can then install it face to face.
why: Word of mouth through masjids and halaqas is how no-ad apps spread. With no ad budget, the noticeboard is the channel.

title: Ask for a review only after real use
what: After the third completed surah or the first finished khatm-by-link, show one dismissible glass card: 'If the app has helped, a review helps others find it', linking to the Play listing (market:// intent from the TWA). Never show it during recitation, and never more than twice.
why: Rating volume drives Play ranking. Ayah's 4.8 from 110k reviews (https://apps.appfollow.io/ios/ayah-quran-app/706037876?country=us) is the bar. Asking at a point of real value, never mid-recitation, keeps it respectful.

title: Open-source and IzzyOnDroid listing as a trust signal
what: Publish the repository with a clear README and licence notes (NOTICES.md already exists). Submit an APK to the IzzyOnDroid repo, add a 'Source code' link in More, and link the CSP-based Data Safety claim to the code.
why: 'Help with placing software on F-droid' is quran_android's most-commented open issue (#755, 77 comments, https://github.com/quran/quran_android/issues). Privacy-minded Muslims actively look for FOSS Quran apps such as QuranApp (https://github.com/alfaazplus/QuranApp).

title: Tablet and landscape two-page spread
what: When the viewport is wider than about 900 px, or in landscape, PagedMushaf shows the facing pages (even on the right in RTL) like a printed mushaf, with the page turn moving both. Put it on a reading-stand-friendly layout with the dock auto-hidden.
why: Qiyam-focused apps such as Mushaf al-Qiyam (https://apps.apple.com/app/id1530008007) exist precisely for tablets on a stand during Taraweeh. desktop.css exists, but the mushaf itself still renders single-page.

title: Public changelog and roadmap with a feedback channel
what: A 'What's new' sheet appears once after an update, with three plain lines and a link to a public roadmap page (docs/roadmap.md rendered on GitHub Pages) plus a GitHub Discussions or email link for requests.
why: Quran.com runs a public board (https://feedback.quran.com/feature-requests) and users engage with it heavily. Showing that requests are heard turns reviewers into advocates and channels complaints away from 1-star reviews.

title: Tajweed colours in the translation view
what: Reuse the existing tajweed.json and src/mushaf/tajweed.ts colouring as a toggle on the live Translation tab's Arabic line, since the mushaf tabs (which use it) are held back in production. Add a small colour legend sheet.
why: 'Support Tajweed Color Quran مصحف التجويد الملون' is quran_android #1353 with 11 comments (https://github.com/quran/quran_android/issues). It ships something already built to the tab that is actually live.
